analysis.summary: Colombia enter as clear favorites on the back of a convincing 3-1 win over Uzbekistan in MD1, sitting top of Group K with a full complement of stars including James Rodriguez and Luis Diaz both in form. DR Congo earned a remarkable 1-1 draw with Portugal in their historic World Cup return, with Yoane Wissa's first-half equalizer showing their counter-attacking threat is real. Colombia need only a draw to secure qualification but their aggressive 4-2-3-1 setup under Lorenzo means they will look to win; DR Congo must avoid defeat to keep advancement alive. The match is played at Estadio Akron in Guadalajara at moderate altitude (1,560m), a setting that suits the South American side more than the African one.
analysis.home_form: Colombia arrive in excellent shape: W3-D0-L2 in their last five competitive matches, scoring 10 and conceding 7. Recent results include a 3-1 win over Costa Rica, a 2-0 win over Jordan, a 2-1 friendly loss to Croatia, a 1-3 loss to France, and most recently a 3-1 World Cup Group K win over Uzbekistan (goals from Munoz, Diaz, Campaz). James Rodriguez pulled strings at No.10 and Luis Diaz was their most dangerous outlet. No confirmed injuries or suspensions affecting the first-choice XI.
analysis.away_form: DR Congo's last five matches: D1-1 Portugal (WC MD1), L1-2 Chile (friendly), D0-0 Denmark AET (friendly/playoff), W1-0 Jamaica (inter-confederation playoff), W2-0 Bermuda (qualifier). They qualified via an inter-confederation playoff and showed resilience against Portugal, taking the lead into half-time through Wissa's header. Defender Rocky Bushiri withdrew injured pre-tournament and was replaced by Aaron Tshibola. Captain Chancel Mbemba (107 caps) leads a disciplined back line that includes Aaron Wan-Bissaka. No confirmed suspensions from MD1.
analysis.h2h: Colombia and DR Congo have never met in recorded international history before this World Cup 2026 fixture. This is the first all-time meeting between the two nations, making direct head-to-head data unavailable as a reference point.
injuries_news: Colombia: No confirmed injuries or suspensions reported. Full first-choice squad expected to be available.

DR Congo: Rocky Bushiri (defender) withdrew injured pre-tournament and was replaced in the squad by Aaron Tshibola. Yoane Wissa returned from a difficult injury-affected club season but started and scored vs Portugal; his fitness appears confirmed.
key_factors: Colombia only need a draw to advance but their high-press 4-2-3-1 system under Lorenzo is inherently attacking, so expect them to push for a win and set the tempo from the start.
DR Congo must avoid defeat to keep their qualification hopes alive, creating a situation where they need to attack, which could open the game up and play into Colombia's counter-pressing strengths.

James Rodriguez as the fulcrum of Colombia's attack is the key tactical battle: if DR Congo's compact midfield (Moutoussamy, Pickel, Kayembe) can stifle him, they limit Colombia's creativity significantly.
Yoane Wissa is DR Congo's primary counter-attacking weapon; Colombia's central defenders Davinson Sanchez and Lucumi must handle his movement and physicality.

Estadio Akron sits at approximately 1,560m altitude — moderate but non-trivial, historically more familiar to South American sides from altitude-acclimatized qualifying environments. Both teams had six days rest since MD1.
Colombia's goal difference (+2) means a win here almost certainly secures Group K top spot ahead of the Portugal-Uzbekistan result, adding further incentive to attack.
